input: What is the refund rate for Home category products?

expected_result.derivation: Similar to sql-01: approved refunded units divided by units sold. psql: 2 / 24 = 0.0833, checked by hand against the 23 raw Home rows. Wrong reading: refund count over row count instead of units = 3 / 23 = 0.1304. Tolerance 0.01 - the two answers are far enough apart that rounding can't explain the gap.
expected_result.review_note: Same root cause as sql-01: generated SQL counts order_item rows instead of unit quantity, and also doesn't filter refunds to approved-only, confirmed by reading the generated SQL directly.

generated_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT r.id) AS total_refunds, COUNT(DISTINCT oi.id) AS total_order_items, ROUND(CAST(COUNT(DISTINCT r.id) * 100.0 / COUNT(DISTINCT oi.id) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS refund_rate_pct FROM order_items AS oi JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.id LEFT JOIN refunds AS r ON oi.id = r.order_item_id WHERE p.category = 'Home' LIMIT 500
failed_checks: Same root cause as sql-01: generated SQL counts order_item rows instead of unit quantity, and also doesn't filter refunds to approved-only, confirmed by reading the generated SQL directly.
